lessons.title: Array transforms and key preservation
lessons.summary: If the predicate keeps odd values, which keys and values print?
explanation: array_filter with an explicit callback keeps entries whose values satisfy that callback. It preserves the original keys rather than rebuilding zero-based indexes. Without a callback its truthiness policy can drop zero, so name the rule deliberately.

array_values returns the values under consecutive integer keys. PHP arrays support both maps and lists; preserving keys matters when preparing a JSON list or indexing by position. array_keys returns the key list, and implode joins a list of values using the supplied separator. These functions return results without changing the original variable.

Expected output or behavior: 10,30
2,4. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Apply array_values to a filtered array and explain when key preservation matters. You may trace it without a PHP interpreter; reading completion is not proof of a local run.

lessons.summary: If the text is A&B, what is the escaped HTML text?

This pure function first checks the minutes field is a String, then validates an integer from 1 through 60 using the filter extension. Treating all request values as trustworthy scalars can cause type errors or bypass intended rules.

The return value explicitly contains status, headers and body. The CLI fixture inspects that contract only: it does not call header(), emit a browser response or verify a server adapter. A web adapter must apply status and headers before body output; authentication and CSRF checks are additional concerns.

{"minutes":15}. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

lessons.title: Sessions cookies and deployment boundaries
lessons.summary: If minutes is unset before saving, what is read after reopening?
explanation: The session extension persists server-side data associated with an identifier; the cookie normally carries that identifier, not the entire session array. The $_SESSION superglobal array holds the active session data; unset($_SESSION["minutes"]) removes that key. session_start acquires state, and session_write_close saves it and releases the lock. Avoid retaining a session lock while unrelated slow work runs.

This isolated CLI fixture disables cookie emission, uses a private disposable file directory, writes state, closes and reopens the same session, then destroys it. Cookie settings are discussed separately, not applied to this cookie-disabled CLI session or browser-verified. In a web integration with cookies enabled, configure session_set_cookie_params with secure=true, httponly=true and the chosen samesite value before session_start; verify its actual Set-Cookie and browser behavior. Real HTTPS deployments must choose Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite, strict-mode and identifier-regeneration policy, prevent fixation and protect state-changing requests; SameSite alone is not a complete CSRF defense.
Expected output or behavior: 15. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

lessons.title: SQL parameters and database boundaries
lessons.summary: If the topic contains SQL-looking text with a quote and DROP TABLE, what does the bound insertion do?
explanation: PDO prepared statements separate SQL structure from parameter data. A placeholder represents a value, not a table name, column identifier or arbitrary SQL fragment. Dynamic identifiers require a separate trusted allowlist. Parameter binding does not replace domain validation or database permissions.

in_array with its third argument true uses strict matching in the driver availability check. This fixture requires PDO plus pdo_sqlite and uses a real SQLite in-memory database, not a pretend query result or external service. Exception mode exposes database failures. Here exec creates the known table, prepare fixes the INSERT template, execute supplies its bound values, query runs SELECT to read data, and fetchColumn retrieves the first column from a result row. The stored value is read back exactly, and a second query confirms the table still exists. This does not establish compatibility with a production MySQL or PostgreSQL deployment.

Expected output or behavior: 1
stored as data. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

lessons.title: Fibers and cooperative suspension
lessons.summary: If resume supplies next instead of ok, what is the final return value?
explanation: Fiber receives a callback. start begins it and returns the value passed to Fiber::suspend; resume continues execution and supplies a value back to that suspension point. This is explicit cooperative control transfer, not parallel execution.

After the callback terminates, getReturn obtains its return value. resume itself does not return that final callback value in this example. Fibers do not make blocking file or network calls nonblocking and do not install an asynchronous runtime automatically.

Expected output or behavior: paused
done:ok. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

lessons.title: Serialization boundaries and untrusted input
lessons.summary: If minutes is a JSON string rather than a JSON number, what happens?
explanation: unserialize can instantiate objects and invoke magic-method behavior. Do not pass untrusted input to it; restricting allowed_classes is not a general validation or security solution. A serialized PHP object graph is not an interchangeable safe data format.

This example uses JSON with exceptions and requires a minutes integer in 1 through 60. JSON avoids PHP object-instantiation behavior but does not remove the need for size limits, depth policy and schema validation. The fixture uses one tiny literal, not arbitrary unbounded input.
Expected output or behavior: 15. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

lessons.title: A bounded study-log pipeline
lessons.summary: If the first text becomes 70, what is collected and summed?
explanation: This fixed list contains four strings. FILTER_VALIDATE_INT checks representability and the 1-through-60 range, with false checked strictly. Invalid inputs are deliberately skipped rather than turned into legitimate zero-minute records.

continue skips the rest of the current iteration, while break exits the loop. The loop stops after two accepted values. Appending with [] creates consecutive keys, so JSON encodes a list. The total is at most 120. This is an in-memory study-log exercise, not durable storage or a production reporting policy for rejected input.
